h1: LIC vs PPF – Which is Best for You?
top_cta: Choosing between a Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) policy and the Public Provident Fund (PPF) depends heavily on your financial goals. While LIC offers a mix of life cover and savings, PPF focuses purely on safe, tax-free wealth accumulation. Start by using our free LIC vs PPF Returns Calculator below to compare projected maturity amounts instantly.

sections.title: What is LIC? (Overview of LIC Policy)

content.text: LIC (Life Insurance Corporation of India) is a state-owned life insurance company offering various endowment and insurance plans. An LIC plan combines life cover with a savings component. You pay annual premiums, and on policy maturity (or death), LIC pays out the sum assured plus accumulated bonuses. Importantly, the core sum assured you choose is secure and guaranteed by the government (under the LIC Act, Sec. 37).

items: Premiums & Coverage: You commit to paying a fixed premium (e.g. ₹50,000/year) for a term (often 15–25 years). You get life cover; if anything happens, dependents get at least the sum assured plus bonuses.

Returns (Bonuses): Because part of your premium pays for insurance and expenses, the effective returns on LIC endowment plans are typically in the 4–6% range. Bonuses are not guaranteed but are historically stable.
Tax Benefits: LIC premiums are tax-deductible under Section 80C (up to ₹1.5L/year). The maturity proceeds and death benefits are tax-free under Section 10(10D) if the premium is ≤ 10% of sum assured.
Suitability: LIC is best when insurance cover is a priority alongside disciplined savings.

content.text: The Public Provident Fund (PPF) is a long-term savings scheme launched by the Government in 1968. It’s 100% government-backed, so your deposits earn a fixed interest rate (currently 7.1% p.a.). PPF is not an insurance or mutual fund – it’s a social security saving vehicle with massive tax benefits.

items: Returns: The PPF rate is reviewed every quarter (currently 7.1%). Because it compounds annually, your investment doubles roughly every 10 years.
Tax Benefits (EEE): PPF is “Exempt-Exempt-Exempt”. Your contributions are deductible under 80C, the interest is entirely tax-free, and the final maturity amount is also 100% tax-free.
Lock-in & Liquidity: PPF has a 15-year lock-in (extendable in 5-year blocks). Partial withdrawals are allowed from the 7th year, and loans can be taken from the 3rd to 6th year.
Suitability: PPF is ideal for long-term goal savings like retirement or a child’s future education. Since there’s no life cover, it’s purely for wealth accumulation.

content.footer: Note: LIC returns are illustrative based on historical bonus rates. PPF rates are subject to quarterly government review.

content.text: Purely from a returns standpoint, PPF wins. It compounds at a higher rate and the entire amount is tax-free. LIC’s advantage is the life cover – your dependents get the sum assured if you pass away early.
Advantages of LIC: Life cover for your family, disciplined forced savings, guaranteed sum assured, and loan options against the policy.
Disadvantages of LIC: Lower returns (~4-6%) which may not beat inflation, poor liquidity in early years, and complex fee structures (commissions).
Advantages of PPF: High guaranteed returns (~7.1%), absolute safety (government backed), and EEE tax-free status on the entire corpus.
Disadvantages of PPF: 15-year long lock-in, ₹1.5L/year contribution limit, and absolutely no insurance or life cover.

items: If You Need Life Insurance + Savings: LIC policies are tailored for those who want protection plus savings (e.g., young parents ensuring their child's future even if the parent passes away).
If You Want Safe, Tax-Free Growth: PPF is better if your priority is maximizing corpus with no risk. For goals like retirement or a child’s education fund, PPF often outperforms LIC significantly.
The Best Strategy: For most investors, a smart approach is to max out PPF for savings and returns, and separately buy a pure Term Life Insurance policy for high-coverage protection at a low cost.

items.q: Which is better, LIC or PPF?
items.a: For pure returns, PPF is better. It offers ~7.1% guaranteed returns, compounded tax-free, making it superior to LIC’s typical 4–6%. But LIC gives life insurance cover too. If your goal is wealth accumulation, PPF wins; if you need insurance plus savings, LIC suits.

items.q: What are the tax benefits of PPF vs LIC?
items.a: Both fall under Section 80C. LIC premiums are deductible, and maturity proceeds are tax-free under 10(10D) if the premium is ≤10% of the sum assured. PPF contributions are also 80C-deductible; importantly, PPF interest and final corpus are fully tax-free (EEE status).

items.q: Which is better for retirement, LIC or PPF?
items.a: Typically PPF. It locks in money for the long term, provides guaranteed growth, and a tax-free corpus – ideal for building a retirement fund. LIC’s lower returns mean they’re less effective for pure retirement savings unless you also need life cover.

items.q: Can I invest in both LIC and PPF?
items.a: Yes. They serve different purposes. Many people invest in PPF for the best post-tax returns and still buy a pure term insurance for life cover. Buying an LIC plan solely as an investment is often not optimal.

items.q: How does liquidity compare between LIC and PPF?
items.a: PPF funds are locked for 15 years (with partial withdrawal allowed after year 7). LIC plans typically require you to pay at least 5 years of premium; you can surrender earlier, but the payout is usually much lower than premiums paid.
